topics.title: Nārāyaṇa and Jyotiṣa
topics.intro: Śrīman Nārāyaṇa / Viṣṇu / Kṛṣṇa alone is the controller of karma—the basis of Jyotiṣa—yet He Himself is untouched by karma. Planetary remedies manage fruits; surrender to Nārāyaṇa addresses the root.

entries.title: The Lord is not bound by karma
entries.sanskrit:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛhā |
iti māṃ yo 'bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate ||
entries.translation: Actions do not taint Me, nor have I longing for the fruits of action. One who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.
entries.note: He who awards the fruits of karma is Himself free of it—a status that belongs to none else.

entries.title: Supervisor of all activity
entries.sanskrit:
na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya |
udāsīnavad āsīnam asaktaṃ teṣu karmasu ||
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-carācaram |
hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate ||
entries.translation: These actions do not bind Me, O Dhanañjaya, for I remain as one indifferent, unattached to those actions. Under My supervision, prakṛti brings forth the moving and the unmoving; by this cause, O son of Kuntī, the world revolves.
entries.note: Jyotiṣa maps the unfolding of destinies under His oversight; He remains the adhyakṣa.

entries.title: Ādi-puruṣa, source of all
entries.sanskrit:
oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya |
janmādy asya yato 'nvayād itarataś cārtheṣv abhijñaḥ svarāṭ |
entries.translation: Obeisance to Bhagavān Vāsudeva—He from whom the creation, maintenance and dissolution of this universe proceed; who is fully cognizant, both directly and indirectly, of all objects, and who is independent.
entries.note: Nārāyaṇa is the origin and knower; charts describe His administration of karma, not a rival power.

topics.title: Types of karma
topics.intro: Vedānta classifies karma as sañcita (stored), prārabdha (already begun to fructify—what the birth chart mainly shows), and āgāmi (yet to be made). The path is: do good deeds, turn from binding action through devotion and knowledge, and ultimately attain mokṣa by the Lord’s grace.

entries.title: Prārabdha and the chart
entries.sanskrit:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthag-vidham |
vividhāś ca pṛthak ceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam ||
entries.translation: The seat (body), the doer, the various instruments, the distinct efforts of many kinds, and Destiny (daiva) as the fifth—these are the factors of action.
entries.note: Daiva/prārabdha appears in the horoscope. Sañcita waits; āgāmi is shaped by present choice and the Lord’s grace.

entries.title: Act without attachment to fruits
entries.sanskrit:
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi ||
entries.translation: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Let not the fruits of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
entries.note: Good deeds as duty and kainkaryam—not as bargaining with grahas—reduce binding and please Nārāyaṇa.

entries.title: The fire that burns stored karma
entries.sanskrit:
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna |
jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||
entries.translation: As a blazing fire turns firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge turns all karma to ashes.
entries.note: Sañcita, the stored karma, is not beyond reach: it can be burnt before it ever ripens.

entries.title: Freedom through surrender
entries.sanskrit: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
entries.translation: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone…
entries.note: Nitya-karmas and puṇya prepare; mokṣa itself is by Nyāsa and the Lord’s grace—see the Nyāsa Vidya topic.

topics.title: Good deeds & nitya-karmas
topics.intro: Śāstra-prescribed puṇya and nitya/naimittika duties purify and prepare; they do not replace śaraṇāgati. Sandhyā, Veda pārāyaṇam and related vaidika nityānuṣṭhānam apply to those with upanayana among the dvija varṇas (Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya). Charity and many forms of kainkaryam apply more broadly.

entries.title: Upanayana saṃskāra (prerequisite)
entries.sanskrit:
garbhāṣṭame 'bde kurvīta brāhmaṇasyaupanāyanam |
garbhād ekādaśe rājño garbhāt tu dvādaśe viśaḥ ||
entries.translation: In the eighth year from conception one should perform the upanayana of a Brāhmaṇa; in the eleventh for a Kṣatriya; in the twelfth for a Vaiśya.
entries.note: Vedādhyayana, Sandhyā and āhitāgni duties begin after upanayana. Those without this adhikāra see the next topic (stotra & seva).

entries.title: Nitya anuṣṭhānam
entries.sanskrit:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ |
śarīra-yātrāpi ca te na prasidhyed akarmaṇaḥ ||
entries.translation: Perform your ordained duty, for action is better than inaction; even the maintenance of your body would not be accomplished through inaction.
entries.note: Daily ordained duties (tri-kāla sandhyā as the spine, snāna, japa, tarpaṇa as applicable) are niyataṃ karma—distinct from mere kāmya rites.

entries.title: Sandhyā Vandanam
entries.sanskrit:
pūrvāṃ sandhyāṃ japaṃs tiṣṭhet sāvitrīm ārka-darśanāt |
pāścimāṃ tu samāsīnaḥ samyag ṛkṣa-vibhāvanāt ||
entries.translation: Standing, one should recite the Sāvitrī at the morning sandhyā until the sun is seen; seated, at the evening sandhyā until the stars appear clearly.
entries.note: For eligible Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas after upanayana. Neglect of sandhyā is condemned in Dharma-śāstra; perform under ācārya guidance.

entries.title: Homas / yajña
entries.sanskrit:
daivam evāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati ||
entries.translation: Some yogins worship the gods with sacrifice; others offer the sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman by means of sacrifice.
entries.note: Agnihotra, aupāsana and occasional iṣṭi belong to those with adhikāra (āhitāgni / gṛhastha with fire). Vaiṣṇava homa and yajña as kainkaryam please Nārāyaṇa when done as His worship.

entries.title: Dāna (charity)
entries.sanskrit:
dātavyam iti yad dānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam ||
entries.translation: Charity given because it ought to be given, to one who cannot return it, in the proper place and time and to a worthy recipient—that gift is remembered as sāttvika.
entries.note: Dāna is universal—not limited to one varṇa. Anna-dāna, go-dāna and vidyā-dāna are especially praised in the Bhāgavatam and Mahābhārata.

entries.title: Veda pārāyaṇam / svādhyāya
entries.sanskrit: svādhyāyān mā pramadaḥ |
entries.translation: Do not neglect the study and recitation of the Veda (svādhyāya).
entries.note: For the upanīta taught by an ācārya. Others may hear Veda-pārāyaṇam and support it as kainkaryam without claiming mantra-adhikāra.

entries.title: These deeds and mokṣa
entries.translation: Nitya-karmas and puṇya reduce binding, accumulate merit and please the Lord. Mokṣa itself is still primarily through Nyāsa / the Lord’s grace.
entries.note: Cross-link: open the Nyāsa Vidya section for the carama ślokas and Mahā Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad on Nyāsa.

topics.title: Stotra, grantha & seva (for all)
topics.intro: If Sandhyā, Veda or homa are not one’s adhikāra, śāstra and sampradāya still offer abundant paths. These are first-class Primary practices—especially in Śrī Vaiṣṇava teaching, where Divya Prabandham stands with the Vedas as Drāviḍa Veda.

entries.title: Viṣṇu Sahasranāma
entries.sanskrit:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ yaś cāpi parikīrtayet |
nāśubhaṃ prāpnuyāt kiñcit so 'mutreha ca mānavaḥ ||
entries.translation: Whoever hears this constantly and whoever also recites it obtains nothing inauspicious—neither here nor in the next world.
entries.note: Open to all who approach with śraddhā. Learn and recite the thousand names of Viṣṇu.

entries.title: Tiruppāvai
entries.sanskrit:
ciṟṟañ ciṟu kāle vandunnai sēvitthu…
unakkē nām āṭ ceyvōm…
entries.translation: (Sense:) In the early dawn we came and worshipped You… We shall perform service only unto You…
entries.note: Nityānusandhānam in Śrī Vaiṣṇava homes, especially in Dhanur-māsa. Surrender to Kaṇṇan / Nārāyaṇa in Tamil Veda.

entries.title: Nālāyira Divya Prabandham
entries.sanskrit:
aṉṟivvulakam aḷantāy aṭiyiṉai…
un caraṇē caraṇam…
entries.translation: (Sense:) O You who measured the worlds—Your feet are my refuge; I take refuge in Your feet alone.
entries.note: In the sampradāya the Divya Prabandham is Drāviḍa Veda—equal in status for instruction in bhakti and śaraṇāgati.

entries.title: Hanumān Cālīsā
entries.sanskrit:
jo nita paṭhai hanumāna cālīsā |
hoya siddhi sākhī gaurīsā ||
entries.translation: Whoever recites the Hanumān Cālīsā daily obtains accomplishment—Gaurīśa (Śiva) is witness.
entries.note: Accessible nāma-stotra praising Rāma-bhakta Hanumān. A popular practice of remembrance; not claimed here as Vedic śruti.

entries.title: Rāmāyaṇa — hearing and reading
entries.sanskrit:
idaṃ pavitraṃ pāpaghnaṃ puṇyaṃ vedaiś ca sammitam |
yaḥ paṭhed rāma-caritaṃ sarva-pāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
entries.translation: This (Rāmāyaṇa) is purifying, sin-destroying, meritorious and equal to the Vedas; whoever reads the deeds of Rāma is freed from all sins.
entries.note: Hearing, reading and pārāyaṇam of the Rāmāyaṇa purify. Pair with the Rāma carama śloka in Nyāsa Vidya.

entries.title: Mahābhārata — hearing and study
entries.citation: Ādi Parva (traditional itihāsa-praśaṃsā); contains Gītā & Sahasranāma
entries.sanskrit:
yo vidyāc caturo vedān sāṅgopaniṣado dvijaḥ |
na cākhyānam idaṃ vidyān naiva sa syād vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
entries.translation: A twice-born who knows the four Vedas with their limbs and Upaniṣads, but does not know this narrative (the Mahābhārata), is not truly wise.
entries.note: Itihāsa-śravaṇa includes the Gītā and Viṣṇu Sahasranāma within the Mahābhārata.

entries.title: Cleaning temples (ālaya-sevā)
entries.citation: Traditional kainkaryam; cf. Bhāgavatam on temple service
entries.sanskrit:
arcāyām eva haraye pūjāṃ yaḥ śraddhayehate |
na tat-parṣadāṃ saṅgaṃ vṛṇīte…
entries.translation: (Sense from Bhāgavata teaching:) One who worships Hari in the arcā with faith… (temple service is beloved kainkaryam).
entries.note: Sweeping, cleaning, lamp-lighting and other ālaya-sevā are physical kainkaryam open to all—service to the Lord’s dwelling.

entries.title: Feeding cows (go-sevā), especially injured
entries.citation: BG 18.44 (kṛṣi-go-rakṣya); Purāṇa praise of go-dāna and go-sevā
entries.sanskrit: kṛṣi-go-rakṣya-vāṇijyaṃ vaiśya-karma svabhāva-jam |
entries.translation: Agriculture, cow-protection and trade are the natural works of the Vaiśya—showing the sacred place of go-rakṣā in dharma.
entries.note: Feeding cows—especially injured or neglected ones—is dayā pleasing to Nārāyaṇa. Universal compassion, not limited by varṇa.

topics.title: Nyāsa Vidya (Rāmānuja Sampradāya)
topics.intro: The Śrī Vaiṣṇava tradition strongly recommends Nyāsa Vidya (śaraṇāgati / prapatti) as the primary, simplest and most straightforward means to mokṣa—among the Brahma Vidyās taught in the Vedas. Swami Vedānta Deśikan’s Nikṣepa Rakṣā defends and clarifies this Nikṣepa / Nyāsa.

entries.title: Nyāsa superior to austerities
entries.sanskrit: tasmāt nyāsam eṣāṃ tapasām atiriktam āhuḥ |
entries.translation: Therefore they declare Nyāsa (self-surrender / renunciation unto the Lord) to be superior to these austerities.
entries.note: After listing satya, tapas, dama, śama, dāna, dharma and other disciplines, the Upaniṣad exalts Nyāsa as foremost.

entries.title: Rāma carama śloka
entries.sanskrit:
sakṛd eva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācate |
abhayaṃ sarva-bhūtebhyo dadāmy etad vrataṃ mama ||
entries.translation: To him who surrenders but once and seeks (saying) ‘I am Yours,’ I grant fearlessness from all beings—this is My vow.
entries.note: Śrī Rāma’s pledge of protection to the prapanna—foundation of śaraṇāgati in the Rāmāyaṇa.

entries.title: Kṛṣṇa carama śloka
entries.sanskrit:
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
ahaṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
entries.translation: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.
entries.note: The carama-śloka of the Gītā—Kṛṣṇa’s final assurance of mokṣa through exclusive śaraṇāgati.

entries.title: Nikṣepa Rakṣā — Vedānta Deśikan
entries.translation: Nikṣepa Rakṣā (‘Protection of the Deposit’) is Deśikan’s treatise defending Nikṣepa / Nyāsa (śaraṇāgati) as the secure, śāstra-backed means of mokṣa—clarifying its nature, adhikāra and relation to bhakti-yoga.
entries.note: Study under a qualified ācārya. This app cites the work; it does not replace sampradāya instruction or formal prapatti.

entries.title: Among the Brahma Vidyās
entries.citation: Upaniṣadic Brahma Vidyās (traditionally counted as thirty-two)
entries.translation: Mokṣa is attained through the Brahma Vidyās taught in the Vedas. In the Rāmānuja sampradāya, Nyāsa Vidya is upheld as the primary and simplest among them for those who take refuge in Śrīman Nārāyaṇa.
entries.note: Nitya-karmas and stotra prepare the heart; Nyāsa is the direct means stressed here.

topics.title: Worship of Śrīman Nārāyaṇa
topics.intro: Broader kainkaryam and bhakti—arcana, nāma-saṅkīrtana, ekādaśī and related rhythms. Stotra lists for those without vaidika adhikāra are in the previous topic.

entries.title: Even a leaf offered with devotion
entries.sanskrit:
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
tad ahaṃ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ||
entries.translation: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water—that offering of devotion from a pure-hearted soul I accept.
entries.note: Arcana is open according to capacity; devotion matters more than grandeur.

entries.title: Fix the mind on Me
entries.sanskrit:
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṃ namaskuru |
mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam ātmānaṃ mat-parāyaṇaḥ ||
entries.translation: Fix your mind on Me, be My devotee, sacrifice to Me, bow to Me; thus disciplined and intent on Me as the supreme goal, you shall come to Me alone.
entries.note: Nāma, arcana, namaskāra and ekādaśī-vrata are living expressions of this verse.

entries.title: Nine limbs of bhakti
entries.sanskrit:
śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṃ pāda-sevanam |
arcanaṃ vandanaṃ dāsyaṃ sakhyam ātma-nivedanam ||
entries.translation: Hearing and chanting of Viṣṇu, remembering Him, serving His feet, worship, obeisance, servitude, friendship and self-offering—these are the nine forms of devotion.
entries.note: Ātma-nivedanam aligns with Nyāsa; the other limbs support a life of kainkaryam.

topics.title: Scripture pointers
topics.intro: Curated highlights across itihāsa, Purāṇa, Upaniṣad and Brahma-sūtra teaching on grace and release—not a full corpus.

entries.title: Release by the Lord’s grace
entries.translation: In Rāmānuja’s reading, release (mokṣa) is the fruit of devotion and the Lord’s grace; the sūtras culminate in the liberated soul’s enjoyment of Brahman, not mere isolation.
entries.note: Study Śrī Bhāṣya with an ācārya for full exposition.

entries.title: Nārāyaṇa as supreme
entries.sanskrit: nārāyaṇāya namaḥ |
entries.translation: Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa—celebrated in the Purāṇa as the one reality from whom the worlds proceed and into whom they return.
entries.note: Pair with Bhāgavata and Gītā citations in earlier topics.

entries.title: Divya Prabandham as Drāviḍa Veda
entries.translation: The Nālāyira Divya Prabandham is received as Drāviḍa Veda—authoritative for bhakti and śaraṇāgati alongside Sanskrit śruti in the Rāmānuja tradition.
entries.note: Primary source, not an afterthought—see Stotra & seva.

topics.title: Kāla: time
topics.intro: Time as a form of the Lord, and the day and night of Brahmā.

entries.title: I am Time among measurers
entries.sanskrit:
prahlādaś cāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatām aham |
mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro 'haṃ vainateyaś ca pakṣiṇām ||
entries.translation: Among the Daityas I am Prahlāda; among those that measure, I am Time; among beasts I am the lion, and among birds Garuḍa, son of Vinatā.
entries.note: Kāla is not a power apart from the Lord; Jyotiṣa measures His own unfolding.

entries.title: The day of Brahmā
entries.sanskrit:
sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ |
rātriṃ yuga-sahasrāntāṃ te 'ho-rātra-vido janāḥ ||
entries.translation: Those who know that a day of Brahmā lasts a thousand yugas, and that his night ends after a thousand yugas, truly know day and night.

entries.title: Worlds arise and dissolve
entries.sanskrit:
avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty ahar-āgame |
rātry-āgame pralīyante tatraivāvyakta-saṃjñake ||
entries.translation: At the coming of Brahmā's day all manifest beings arise from the unmanifest; at the coming of his night they dissolve into that same unmanifest.

topics.title: Saṃsāra: the wheel
topics.intro: How the embodied self passes from body to body, and the one way it does not return.

entries.title: Changing bodies like garments
entries.sanskrit:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi |
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī ||
entries.translation: As a person casts off worn-out garments and puts on others that are new, so the embodied self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.

entries.title: The last thought shapes the next birth
entries.sanskrit:
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalevaram |
taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ ||
entries.translation: Whatever state of being one remembers when leaving the body at the end, O son of Kuntī, that state one attains, having always been absorbed in it.

entries.title: Merit spent, the soul returns
entries.sanskrit: te taṃ bhuktvā svarga-lokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṃ viśanti |
entries.translation: Having enjoyed the vast world of heaven, when their merit is exhausted they enter the world of mortals again.
entries.note: Good karma alone does not end the wheel; it only earns a pleasanter turn of it.

entries.title: No return for one who reaches Him
entries.sanskrit:
ā-brahma-bhuvanāl lokāḥ punar āvartino 'rjuna |
mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate ||
entries.translation: All worlds up to the realm of Brahmā are subject to return, O Arjuna; but for one who reaches Me, O son of Kuntī, there is no rebirth.
